incidents.what_happened: A review approval moved a unit to ready-to-merge before the required gates on that exact candidate SHA had completed. A later red candidate was routed to repair. Separately, main-red quarantine compared check names, so the same failing test was missed when the main and PR workflows reported it under different check names.
incidents.root_cause_evidence: Original log: [2026-11-02T22:54:48Z] gated unit=issue-3237 PR#4994 readied on fc53c3cfc; [2026-11-02T23:04:32Z] merge skipped PR#4994 (tests failed in: Touched packages PR gate) -> repair-pending without waiting for the other checks or a rerun. Before the fix, engine/mac-autopilot/scheduler.d/harvest-workers.sh:168 recorded review approval and ready-to-merge before required candidate CI completed; engine/mac-autopilot/scheduler.d/merge-lane.sh:307-317 handled the red candidate later. Before the fix, engine/mac-autopilot/scheduler.d/ci-status.sh:32-63 matched failed check names, while a shared test can be reported under different names in the main and PR checks.
incidents.classic_pattern: An asynchronous prerequisite is checked after a state transition has already granted downstream eligibility; a second control compares presentation labels instead of the underlying failing test identity.
incidents.best_known_solution: Keep approval as durable evidence, store required-gates green bound to the exact PR head SHA, and admit a unit to ready-to-merge only while that bound SHA still matches. Invalidate the evidence on a head change and return a carried approval to CI waiting. For main-red quarantine, parse failed test file and test name from both sides and quarantine only when every candidate test identity is present on main; fail closed when a failed check cannot be identified.
options_considered: Keep the existing review-approve transition and let merge-lane discover a red check later; this still makes the unverified candidate merge-eligible and can send a shared main failure to repair.
Persist a generic green flag on the unit; this can survive a candidate head change and incorrectly authorize a different SHA.
Keep reviewer approval recorded, require all configured required gates to pass on the current approved SHA before ready-to-merge, and clear green evidence whenever that SHA changes; selected.
Continue comparing failed check names; this cannot detect shared test failures reported by differently named checks.
Compare parsed failing test file and test name across candidate and main job logs, and fail closed when a complete identity is unavailable; selected.

siblings.expected_result: Approval remains in ci-pending while candidate checks are red and requests the existing same-SHA retry without repair dispatch; only same-SHA required-gate success reaches ready-to-merge; a head change clears green evidence; no-PR direct-main approval keeps its focused-gate delivery path; a shared test identity is quarantined across different check names; and any unidentifiable failure prevents quarantine.

machine_checks.why: Replays review approval followed by a red required gate on the same candidate SHA, verifies the approval is retained and a bounded same-SHA retry starts without repair dispatch, checks that only same-SHA required-gate success enables ready-to-merge, verifies head changes invalidate green evidence, quarantines one shared failing test reported under differently named checks, rejects quarantine when a mixed-log Node TAP or raw assertion failure lacks identity, and preserves the existing repair escalation after a repeated red.

Plants the pre-fix approval transition and check-name comparison; the replay fails because approval reaches ready-to-merge before candidate CI, and the shared test is not quarantined across different check names.

incidents.what_happened: The 120-second maintenance slice repeatedly timed out or hit its optional-work cutoff before needs-info email polling and reopened-issue recovery could run. The 24-hour timing sample showed hold-sweep at 26 seconds p50 / 35 p90, needs-info-email at 27 / 37, needs-info-recovery at 12 / 16, and blocker-root recovery at 2 / 77.
incidents.root_cause_evidence: Journal line: issue-pipeline: slice tick=20261103T091050Z stage=maintenance elapsed_sec=120 status=124. Before the fix, origin/main at ff12d117bf6d873d0ac9925baa481a7f59abfe5f used one cutoff at engine/issue-pipeline.sh:1226, 1236 and ordered needs-info-email and needs-info-recovery after hold and founder-outcome work at lines 1228-1229. Ownerless held issues also caused point issue views inside the per-hold loop at engine/lib.d/holds.sh:404, 510 in that baseline.
incidents.classic_pattern: Deadline-budget starvation: optional work consumes a shared work-conserving budget before required recovery has an admitted runtime slot. The maintenance loop resembles a soft real-time scheduler with a deadline but no admission control for its critical jobs.
incidents.best_known_solution: Use deadline-aware admission control: reserve the measured runtime for required work, split the email/reopen slot so the email poll's GH, Gmail, and token reads yield at its subdeadline, run reopen recovery with its own remaining slot before the optional suffix, and batch repeated reads. Linux SCHED_DEADLINE documents admitted runtime within a deadline; Google SRE overload guidance recommends rejecting or shedding noncritical work early to protect critical paths.
options_considered: Increase the 120-second slice limit; this hides the overrun and still permits optional work to consume the entire enlarged budget.
Increase the generic step reserve while keeping required recovery behind the same optional sequence; an in-flight optional read can still cross the reserve boundary.

Reserve 55 seconds from measured email and reopen p90s, split it into a bounded 37-second email slot and an 18-second reopen slot, bound prefix optional GitHub reads at the earlier cutoff, run required recovery before the optional suffix, and keep the existing 15-second hard-timeout reserve; selected.
Batch the hold sweep's issue detail reads so ownerless holds no longer add one point query per issue; selected as a direct reduction of measured recurring work.

machine_checks.why: Plants the pre-fix cutoff and ordering with an earlier maintenance section that consumes the remaining budget; the required email and reopen calls are absent.

The email subslot is bounded by the absolute GH/Gmail deadline and yields at the cutoff; stubs simulate the measured 37s + 16s p90 pair, confirm reopen keeps its 18s slot before the 105s cutoff, then check the three-tick warning and #166 scheduler signature.
Four ownerless holds reuse the detailed batch snapshot with no per-issue GitHub views.
A threshold maintenance deferral is filed through the normal bell #166 issue-upsert path and duplicate signatures are suppressed.

incidents.what_happened: Advisor jobs had terminal failures recorded in answer.err, but the incident intake watched only node_health's six-hour successful-answer-age threshold. A red post-merge main CI run likewise had no incident path. The result was a many-hour gap between advisor failures and an issue being filed.
incidents.root_cause_evidence: A redacted captured answer.err line has the shape '[redacted-provider] ADVISOR_ANSWER_TIMEOUT: <redacted diagnostic>' (engine/mac-autopilot/fixtures/advisor-timeout-prefixed.answer.err). On origin/main, engine/providers/web-advisor-provider.sh:638-648 deleted terminal job data after returning only a raw error tail or parsed answer; engine/run-advisor-batch.sh:433-446 recorded outcome and job identity without diagnostic codes; engine/mac-autopilot/bell.sh:378-426 consumed incremental scheduler.log lines and changed alert files but never scanned advisor-batch result records. engine/mac-autopilot/node_health.py:83 marked advisor answer age unhealthy only at six hours. The same bell had a main CI run snapshot for queue handling but did not turn completed red runs into incidents.
incidents.classic_pattern: A producer discards machine-readable failure meaning before cleanup, while a downstream health aggregate observes only delayed absence of success; durable terminal events have no incident owner.
incidents.best_known_solution: Extract the three required ADVISOR_* codes and the safe picker-not-found class before provider job cleanup, persist them with each advisor batch result, and scan those results from the existing bell tick using stable #166 signatures. Use the same bell tick's main CI snapshot plus the existing bounded gh wrapper and CI test-log parser to file red-run incidents keyed by check and first test. Keep recovery quiet when a later success breaks a consecutive-failure streak.
options_considered: Lower the six-hour node-health threshold; rejected because it still waits on an aggregate symptom and cannot identify a terminal error or red CI check.
Add another polling daemon; rejected because it adds a second schedule and incident owner while the bell already owns #166 upsert and dedupe.

Capture durable advisor diagnostics and inspect advisor results plus the existing CI snapshot in one bell scan; selected because failure detection uses the event already emitted and reuses #166 hashing, severity and upsert.

siblings.expected_result: Three redacted answer.err shapes yield one issue per required signature in one scan; the planted pre-fix bell misses a timeout; isolated fail-then-success is quiet; picker fallback and red/green main CI fixtures follow the same intake.

machine_checks.why: Replays three redacted real answer.err shapes, checks pending-job diagnostics survive, verifies fail streak and recovery behavior, and exercises picker fallback plus red/green main CI incident intake.
Removes the new bell scan calls to plant the pre-fix behavior; a real redacted timeout result is missed and the guard reports the expected failure.

incidents.what_happened: Four ready-to-merge hotpatch units (release-blocker PRs on hotfix/* branches) stayed on draft PRs for hours while 5 of 12 PR runners idled; every slow tick logged merge skipped PR#<n> (draft, waiting for its CI slot) and no admission path flipped them.
incidents.root_cause_evidence: Live scheduler.log 2026-11-03T05:24:24Z repeats merge skipped PR#4938/4940/4942/4921 (draft, waiting for its CI slot); the PRs carry no agent/ci-gated label, so gated_ready returned at the [[ -n "$pr" ]] || return 0 guard (engine/mac-autopilot/scheduler.d/ci-status.sh:371 pre-fix) while the WIP selection excludes them via (.hotpatch // false) != true (engine/mac-autopilot/scheduler.d/ci-admission.sh:156): the two selectors have an empty intersection, so no code path could ever ready them.
incidents.classic_pattern: A membership-gated handler returns success without acting (silent no-op), and the population it silently drops is excluded from every other path by a disjoint predicate: starvation with all capacity idle.
incidents.best_known_solution: A single admission decision point must resolve PR draft/head state from the full PR census when the gated-label census does not index the unit, and a symptom watch must alert when a ready-to-merge draft waits past a bound while free slots exist.
options_considered: Add the gated label to hotfix PRs at orphan adoption; this repairs one registration path but any other unlabeled draft source starves the same way.
Drop the hotpatch exclusion so hotpatches take product CI slots; this inverts the hotfix exemption design and queues hotfixes behind product CI.
Resolve draft/head from the full per-tick PR census inside gated_ready when the branch is unlabeled, keeping one ready decision point for labeled and unlabeled drafts; selected.
Add ci_slot_starve_watch so any future class of un-readable ready draft alerts within a bounded time while free slots exist; selected as the symptom guard.

siblings.discovery_command: grep -c 'draft, waiting for its CI slot' "$A/scheduler.log" vs gh api runners busy count
siblings.expected_result: Zero ready-to-merge drafts remain after an admission pass with free slots; CI-SLOT-STARVE alerts otherwise.

machine_checks.why: Replays the live four-unit unlabeled-draft population through ci_admission: all readied in one pass with 5 free slots, starvation watch alerts after three slow admission ticks with free slots and stays silent at zero free slots, and the per-pass slot_sync and product-path lookup bounds hold.
Plants the verbatim pre-fix gated_ready and proves the replay detects the un-readied drafts (fail against the real past bad code) and starts the starvation clock.

incidents.what_happened: Issue #156 used an unbalanced pattern in a jq test() filter. Fixtures reached it only when one specific history entry existed, so ordinary coverage missed the syntax error.
incidents.root_cause_evidence: Issue #156 was fixed in commit 22e253d with a scheduler regression case; the pattern can be compiled directly with jq.
incidents.classic_pattern: A data-dependent fixture leaves a literal regular expression uncompiled until one exact branch is selected.
incidents.best_known_solution: Compile every literal jq test(), match(), capture(), sub() and gsub() pattern in engine shell files with jq before relying on fixture execution.
options_considered: Add a fixture for the known history entry; this would cover one branch but leave other literal patterns dependent on fixture data.
Compile every literal regex with jq itself; this covers syntax independently of runtime data and was selected.

siblings.expected_result: Every literal jq regex in engine shell files compiles successfully.

machine_checks.why: Compiles engine literals and proves an unbalanced planted pattern is rejected.
Retains the original scheduler regression case.

incidents.what_happened: Issue #157 cached candidate rows containing issue bodies by passing the complete string to jq through --arg. A large intake exceeded the OS argument limit and failed with Argument list too long.
incidents.root_cause_evidence: Issue #157 was fixed in commit e4a748c by streaming the cache rows; scheduler.test.sh adds a fixture over 2 MiB.
incidents.classic_pattern: A growing list or body is bound as one jq argv value; per-argument limits can be exceeded before the program starts.
incidents.best_known_solution: Stream large JSON or prose through stdin or a file, and lint known-unbounded variable names passed to --arg or --argjson.
options_considered: Truncate issue bodies; this loses cache data and does not bound row counts.
Split the cache into multiple argv chunks; this keeps the same fragile transport contract.
Stream the serialized value to jq and flag --arg/--argjson bindings of known unbounded variables; this avoids argv limits and follows the existing lint style, so it was selected.

siblings.expected_result: A rows variable passed through --arg is flagged; fixed stdin streaming passes.

machine_checks.why: Proves a planted --arg rows "$rows" binding is flagged and scans production shell files.
Exercises the #159 large-row cache regression above 2 MiB.

incidents.what_happened: Issue #157's refill path read HANDOFF_PR_CENSUS before assignment under set -u, aborting a tick before existing startable work was dispatched.
incidents.root_cause_evidence: The fix from branch fix/refill-census-unbound merged in pull request #160 as commit c9cb023.
incidents.classic_pattern: A fallback path skips a path-local assignment and later reads an unset variable under nounset.
incidents.best_known_solution: Initialize the census before refill or fallback reads and keep nounset enabled.
options_considered: Disable nounset for the fallback; this suppresses the useful error and lets missing state flow onward.
Initialize the census before every path can read it; this preserves nounset and gives fallback logic a defined empty state, so it was selected.

siblings.expected_result: Refill completes and existing startable work dispatches despite the handoff lookup path.

machine_checks.why: Regression case reaches the refill fallback with set -u and checks dispatch continues.

incidents.what_happened: One gh pr list call hung for 44 minutes until TICK-TIMEOUT; refill remained locked out for 28 minutes.
incidents.root_cause_evidence: The scheduler wrapper called command gh without a timeout; the bounded-wrapper fix is on branch fix/scheduler-gh-timeout.
incidents.classic_pattern: An unbounded network CLI call can keep a scheduler lock longer than the useful work window.
incidents.best_known_solution: Route scheduler gh() through gh_timeout with a validated per-call limit, log timed-out calls, and statically reject direct command gh calls in scheduler and library sources.
options_considered: Raise TICK-TIMEOUT; this lengthens the maximum lockout rather than bounding each network call.
Retry a stalled command; without a deadline this repeats the same unbounded wait.
Use one bounded timeout wrapper for scheduler GitHub calls and fail static checks on direct command gh bypasses; this constrains each call and prevents callsite drift, so it was selected.

siblings.expected_result: No production scheduler/lib shell source calls command gh directly.

machine_checks.why: Checks all scheduler/lib shell sources and proves a planted command gh bypass is rejected.
Times out a stalled gh CLI call, verifies the child is stopped, and checks timeout logging.

incidents.what_happened: A product-pin rollback was refused by publish preflight with resolved-config-check: CHANGED, leaving a broken engine live.
incidents.root_cause_evidence: The preflight did not recognize the explicit rollback path; the engine-swap canary fix is on branch feat/engine-swap-canary.
incidents.classic_pattern: A broad safety preflight blocks a narrowly authorized recovery change because the recovery path is not modeled as an allowed transition.
incidents.best_known_solution: Keep ordinary changed-config checks, while allowing only an explicit verified engine-swap/canary path to carry the product pin change.
options_considered: Skip preflight for every rollback; this would permit unrelated resolved-config drift.
Leave the old engine live until a fresh forward release is ready; this prolongs a known-broken state.
Require a verified engine-swap path for the pin change while preserving ordinary refusal behavior; this keeps the gate and supports controlled recovery, so it was selected.

siblings.expected_result: The verified swap/rollback case passes while unlisted resolved-config changes remain blocked.

machine_checks.why: Exercises engine version selection and publish preflight behavior.
Keeps the default refusal for unlisted resolved-config changes and accepts listed changes with a reason.

incidents.class: optional file reads confused with persistence loss
incidents.what_happened: Intake parsed a missing per-issue JSON file while checking for an optional scheduler handoff. jqf captured jq stderr and logged the missing-file error on every candidate pass, even though the caller redirected stderr and no handoff was expected.
incidents.root_cause_evidence: engine/mac-autopilot/scheduler.d/intake.sh read the candidate state path through jqf without an existence-aware optional-file reader; the runtime scheduler log shows repeated missing-file diagnostics for open ready-for-agent issues. engine/lib.d/issue-state.sh creates per-issue JSON lazily through state_merge and issue_transition, and the repository has no general cleanup for those JSON files.
incidents.classic_pattern: An optional input reaches a parser before absence is modeled, so normal absence is reported as an error and repeated at the call site.
options_considered: Suppress jqf logging globally for missing paths; rejected because missing required inputs would lose their diagnostics.
Add existence checks only at intake call sites; rejected because the same optional-file pattern appears in shared scheduler caches and a check followed by a separate read can race.

Add jqf_optional_file in the shared scheduler core, return a distinct status for true absence, and keep existing paths on jqf; chosen because callers can model absence while malformed and unreadable files remain diagnostic.
incidents.best_known_solution: Route optional scheduler file reads through jqf_optional_file. It returns status 64 without logging only when a path is absent; callers treat that status as an empty optional value, and existing paths still use jqf so parse and read failures are logged.

incidents.what_happened: Every pipeline tick since 2026-11-03 05:23Z was refused: one advisor batch member had a live scheduler worker, pipeline_batch_claim_acquire returned 1, the advisor stage translated it to exit 75, and issue-pipeline-slices.sh counted only 0/124/137 as non-failures, so failed=1 and run-tick refused the tick. The same batch re-triaged two tickets whose scheduler units were in flight, which is what made a member busy in the first place.
incidents.root_cause_evidence: engine/issue-pipeline-slices.sh slice case (pre-fix: '0) ;; 124|137) ... *) failed=1') had no defer arm; engine/issue-pipeline.sh dispatch_advisor_batch claim-unavailable 'return 75'; live journal shows repeated 'run-tick: refusing to run this tick — issue-pipeline.sh exited with status 1' and the live autopilot scheduler.log shows the incident signature matched nothing in engine/mac-autopilot/bell.sh scheduler_signature_class().
incidents.classic_pattern: A component communicates 'temporary, retry later' through a non-zero exit code that an aggregator treats as failure, so a single soft miss is escalated to a whole-system outage; paired with a monitor that only recognizes hard-crash signatures, the outage also files no incident.
incidents.best_known_solution: Keep the stage-exit contract in one place: 75 defers and 124/137 overrun without refusing, while any other unexpected stage status is logged and isolated to that slice. The run-tick checkout gate retains its explicit pre-handoff integrity refusal set. Advisor selection and batch acquisition both consult the scheduler-unit in-flight predicate; claim renewal drops one failed member and keeps the batch running; #166 incident classes include slice and status.
options_considered: Refuse the tick for every unexpected non-zero slice status; rejected because one isolated stage must not prevent other stages or launcher post-steps from running.
Catch 75 at each dispatch call site only; rejected because the stage-exit contract stays implicit and the next defer-producing path re-triggers the outage.
Return success for every non-zero stage status without logging; rejected because unexpected failures would lose their incident evidence.
One explicit stage contract, slice-local failure notes, and a pre-handoff checkout-integrity refusal set; selected because failures stay visible without blocking unrelated work.

siblings.expected_result: A stage exit 1 is recorded while later slices run and the launcher reaches its post-steps; a wrong-branch checkout is still refused.

machine_checks.why: Exercises the real slice runner, advisor batch claim filtering/renewal, in-flight predicates, and slice+status incident identity.

incidents.what_happened: An advisor slice exited 1, then the slice summary returned 1 and run-tick refused the whole factory tick. Later stages and run-tick post-steps were skipped even though only one slice failed.
incidents.root_cause_evidence: Original output: 'issue-pipeline: slice failed stage=advisor status=1; refusing this tick'. The old catch-all arm in engine/issue-pipeline-slices.sh set failed=1 and returned it; engine/run-tick.sh then refused every nonzero issue-pipeline exit before post-handoff work. The exact path is replayed by engine/run-tick-slice-isolation.test.sh.
incidents.classic_pattern: A serial coordinator promotes one worker's local error into a global stop signal, so unrelated stages and cleanup work are skipped even though their inputs remain valid.
incidents.best_known_solution: Treat each slice as an isolation boundary: continue after unexpected statuses, append a durable stage+status line for bell intake, and return success after the full stage list. Keep checkout-integrity checks in run-tick before handoff, with their allowed refusal tags declared alongside the slice contract.
options_considered: Return nonzero after any failed slice; rejected because the launcher then skips independent stage work and its post-handoff checks.
Continue silently and return success; rejected because the bell cannot file a durable incident or dedupe repeats.
Continue, log stage+status, and return success while run-tick guards checkout integrity before handoff; selected because one broken stage cannot stop the rest and its cause remains actionable.

siblings.expected_result: A planted recut exit 1 still runs maintenance and timer post-steps; a wrong-branch checkout exits 1 before the scheduler starts.

machine_checks.why: Asserts an unexpected exit 1 is isolated, later slices run, the summary stays successful, and the incident class contains slice and status.
Runs a local bare-origin launcher fixture and checks post-handoff timer work completes after a slice failure while checkout-integrity failure still refuses.

incidents.what_happened: An issue requeued to rereview-pending retained needs-advisor, entered the advisor batch because selection checked only live workers, and then one claim renewal failure stopped the entire advisor batch and contributed to tick refusal.
incidents.root_cause_evidence: Original output: 'issue-pipeline: batch claim renewal failed; stopping vecta-advisor-batch' followed by 'issue-pipeline: slice failed stage=advisor status=1; refusing this tick'. engine/issue-pipeline.sh selected members using worker/label checks, pipeline_batch_claim_acquire omitted scheduler_issue_unit_inflight, and pipeline_batch_claim_keep stopped the batch on one failed renewal. supervisor_requeue_unit changed the unit stage but did not transition the issue label from needs-advisor. The regressions are planted in engine/tick-refuse-guard.test.sh and engine/mac-autopilot/supervisor-arbiter.test.sh.
incidents.classic_pattern: Two owners make decisions from different projections of the same work item: one reads a stale queue label while the other reads the unit ledger, and a single lease miss is incorrectly handled as a batch-wide failure.
incidents.best_known_solution: Use scheduler_issue_unit_inflight both while selecting advisor candidates and while acquiring batch claims; any nonterminal or pending unit is excluded. If a post-launch renewal misses, release only that member's lease and continue renewing the remaining members. On supervisor requeue, move the issue through the shared ready-for-agent transition so stale needs-advisor and hold labels are cleared with the unit update.
options_considered: Keep checking only worker PIDs and rely on the coordinator lease; rejected because pending scheduler units exist before a PID is visible.
Stop the entire batch after one renewal failure; rejected because the remaining independently claimed members are still valid work.

Share the in-flight predicate across selection and acquisition, drop one failed renewal member, and reconcile labels at supervisor requeue; selected because the ledger, lease, and queue label agree on ownership.

siblings.expected_result: A needs-advisor rereview-pending member is excluded, other members remain claimable after a renewal miss, and supervisor requeue removes the stale needs-advisor label.

machine_checks.why: Covers pending-stage filtering before and during claim acquisition, single-member renewal loss, and continued slice execution.
Replays supervisor requeue from needs-advisor and checks the issue transition removes that stale label and restores ready-for-agent.

incidents.what_happened: Most intake ticks logged 'jqf error (rc=2) in intake_candidates: jq: error: writing output failed: Broken pipe' (69 lines in the live scheduler.log, 2026-10-30 through 2026-11-03, latest 04:01:33Z) and dispatch_supervisor_arbiters the same (16 lines). Consumers stop reading jqf streams early by design - register_new_issues breaks at 'added < want', arbiter dispatch returns at capacity, 'jqf | head -n' bounds rows - and under systemd (SIGPIPE ignored) jq reports the closed pipe as rc=2 with that message, so jqf logged a healthy truncation as an error and buried real ones in scheduler.log, the incident intake and the canary signature baseline (extract_signatures normalizes every jqf error line).
incidents.root_cause_evidence: engine/mac-autopilot/scheduler.d/core.sh jqf() logged every non-zero jq exit whose stderr was non-empty; intake.sh:289 '(( added < want )) || break' closes the candidate stream fed at intake.sh:574 while the producer's jqf is still writing; evals-arbiter.sh dispatch_supervisor_arbiters returns 0 from inside a loop fed by 'done < <(jqf ... "$UNITS")' (evals-arbiter.sh:355). With SIGPIPE ignored (systemd service, command substitution) jq exits 2 with 'jq: error: writing output failed: Broken pipe'; with SIGPIPE default it dies silently with rc=141 and empty stderr, which jqf already did not log.
incidents.classic_pattern: A producer wrapper reports every downstream failure as its own error, so a consumer that stops reading by design (break, return, head) is indistinguishable from a real processing failure in the logs, and the noise hides genuine errors from humans and signature scanners.
incidents.best_known_solution: jqf treats exactly 'writing output failed: Broken pipe' (EPIPE on jq's stdout, only possible when the downstream reader closed) as not an error and skips the log line; every other first-line message - parse and runtime errors, and write failures such as ENOSPC - is still logged. jq's exit code is returned unchanged. One fix in the shared wrapper covers all ~50 'done < <(jqf ...)' consumers; no per-consumer draining.
options_considered: Suppress every rc=2 write failure; rejected because ENOSPC and other real output failures share the exit code.
Drain or bound the candidate stream in intake instead; rejected because it fixes one consumer of ~50 with the same shape and keeps the wrapper lying about the class.
Skip the log line only for the exact EPIPE message; selected: EPIPE on stdout can only mean the consumer closed the pipe, so the carve-out cannot hide a real jq failure.

siblings.expected_result: Early-stopping consumers log no jqf error and real failures still do; every case fails on the pre-fix wrapper (exit 1 on origin/main).

machine_checks.why: Runs the real jqf wrapper with a bounded 'jqf | head' consumer, a read loop that breaks early, a malformed-JSON parse error and an ENOSPC write to /dev/full; the first two must stay silent, the last two must log.
Adjacent contract on the same wrapper: real malformed-state jq failures through register_new_issues keep their jqf diagnostics.

incidents.what_happened: The per-unit advisor launched Node with a bundled provider path based on the engine-live symlink's parent. Node returned MODULE_NOT_FOUND and the unit fell back to arbiter review.
incidents.root_cause_evidence: Original log: Error: Cannot find module '<engine-live>/../.agents/skills/web-advisor-provider/ask.cjs' (MODULE_NOT_FOUND). engine/config.sh:45 kept ZF_ENGINE_DIR logical for live-link behavior, while :112 derived the provider path by appending ../ to that logical path. The planted case in engine/config.test.sh fails on the old derivation.
incidents.classic_pattern: A logical symlink path is used to find a sibling resource with .., so lookup follows the symlink's parent instead of the directory containing the target version.
incidents.best_known_solution: Keep ZF_ENGINE_DIR logical for live-link reload behavior, resolve its physical directory once in engine/config.sh, and derive every parent-relative path from that physical parent. Before launching a unit advisor, require a readable provider; log one stable scheduler line, route to arbiter review, and let the bell file the incident through issue upsert.
options_considered: Make ZF_ENGINE_DIR physical everywhere; this fixes sibling lookup but changes the logical live-link path used by long-running loops after a swap.
Resolve only the provider script at its caller; this leaves ZF_REPO_DIR and any other parent-relative engine defaults exposed to the same symlink error.
Keep ZF_ENGINE_DIR logical and derive one physical parent in config.sh for all parent-relative defaults; selected because it fixes the whole path family while preserving live-link behavior.

siblings.expected_result: The planted engine-live symlink resolves the provider script into the physical version root; the old derivation exits 1 with a path mismatch.

machine_checks.why: Sources config.sh through a symlinked engine with ZF_ENGINE_DIR unset and asserts the provider script resolves inside the physical version root.
Proves an absent provider is routed to arbiter review without launching the advisor, logs one diagnostic, and files one bell incident through the issue-upsert entry point.

incidents.what_happened: A review was configured to use the same Codex family that wrote the head. The old resolver returned the implementer's identity whenever its different-provider review role was unavailable, so the verifier could be from the same family as the worker it reviewed.
incidents.root_cause_evidence: The original scheduler log recorded a review running in the same family as the head author. The pre-fix engine/lib.d/model-policy.sh:761 printed implement_identity after the cross-provider role was unavailable, making the matching family an accepted verifier.
incidents.classic_pattern: A fail-open availability fallback reuses the identity being checked, so a verification control loses independence exactly when its preferred verifier is unavailable. Shared model-family failures then affect both the change and its review.
incidents.best_known_solution: Classify identities in one model-family table and select a reviewer using the model/backend recorded on the unit or its latest implement/repair worker. Codex heads try GLM, then the specifically authorized review_fallback role; GLM heads try Codex, then that same role. Reject same-family candidates and keep the review pending with one #166 bell intake line when all independent reviewers are unavailable.
options_considered: Switch to another model within the Codex family; rejected because the reviewer remains in the writer's family.
Return to the author's identity when GLM is unavailable; rejected because the reviewer loses independence during the exact outage this fallback handles.
Use the independent family first, allow the named review_fallback role only as fallback, then wait and alert; selected because no unavailable-provider path can dispatch the author's family.

siblings.expected_result: The planted pre-fix resolver exits 1 after dispatching a same-family reviewer for its bad config; the fixed dispatcher refuses that config and the full focused guard exits 0.

machine_checks.why: Routes Codex-authored work to GLM and GLM-authored work to Codex, refuses a planted same-family config, tests the named fallback and both-held wait/alert, rejects policy-forbidden implementation models, and requires the planted historical fail-open selector to fail with same-family dispatch evidence.

incidents.what_happened: Incident reports required root-cause and recurrence-guard sections but did not require a researched prior-art section, so a local fix could be approved without identifying the established problem class, expert framing, or mature solutions.
incidents.root_cause_evidence: Before the fix, engine/incident-rule.sh:28-30 required root-cause and recurrence-guard but no prior-art; engine/mac-autopilot/scheduler.d/review-rules.sh:45-46 checked only those two headings, allowing READY without prior-art sources.
incidents.classic_pattern: Incident learning stops at a local corrective action instead of comparing the failure with the known problem class and prior solutions; this is a postmortem and lessons-learned process gap.
incidents.best_known_solution: Use an evidence-based, blameless postmortem to map the incident to a classic problem, compare mature solutions and community practice, and select a preventive action with a verifiable recurrence guard. When evidence is uncertain or conflicting, escalate with a recorded reference rather than guessing.
options_considered: Add only a prompt requirement; this leaves omissions and citation-free claims invisible to the review gate.
Require the prior-art heading but do not inspect its content; an empty section or bare assertion could pass.

Require the section and a source URL in the existing incident report gate, and require a specific escalation reference when an escalation is stated; selected because it makes the evidence checkable without introducing another gate.

siblings.expected_result: Incident reports without prior-art or source URLs are rejected; referenced sources are accepted; non-incident reports are unaffected. The planted prior gate accepts the old-shape report and makes the recurrence assertion fail.

machine_checks.why: Checks prompt instructions, rejection without prior-art, rejection without a source URL, acceptance with source URLs, escalation-reference enforcement, and the non-incident exemption.

Replays the pre-fix gate behavior against the historical report shape that contains root-cause and recurrence-guard but no prior-art; the recurrence assertion fails because the old gate returns READY.

incidents.what_happened: A valid REQUEST-CHANGES review recorded no findings, then a repair delivered no new head. The scheduler still counted its write-start toward stop-loss and the repair cap, and supervisor requeue selected another repair for the unchanged head.
incidents.root_cause_evidence: Original scheduler event: '[2026-11-03T05:52:03Z] repair-no-push: head 6e66bd2a38d04d4551036ba778fccd945b638940 unchanged after repair'. On origin/main, engine/mac-autopilot/scheduler.d/stop-loss.sh:23 and engine/mac-autopilot/scheduler.d/stop-loss.sh:38 counted every write-start without correlating the repair with its triggering review_findings record and later same-SHA repair-no-push outcome; engine/mac-autopilot/scheduler.d/evals-arbiter.sh:374 always selected repair-pending for units with review history and a PR.
incidents.classic_pattern: A retry policy spends a finite failure budget on work that has no actionable input and cannot make progress, then retries the same unchanged state.
incidents.best_known_solution: Correlate each repair start with its recorded review marker and subsequent outcome. Exclude only a valid empty-findings review followed by a same-SHA repair-no-push from failure budgets; route unchanged no-actionable heads and confirmed no-push repairs to a fresh independent review, while retaining ordinary repair counting and repair requeues for real findings.
options_considered: Keep counting every write-start; rejected because it charges an empty, unchanged repair against both stop-loss and repair limits.
Exclude every repair-no-push; rejected because a failed repair with actionable findings still needs to count.
Manually refund a round when the unit reaches supervisor review; rejected because that mutates accounting based on the escalation destination instead of the persisted review and repair outcome.

Correlate the verified empty findings marker, unchanged reviewed SHA, and repair-no-push event; selected because it distinguishes non-progress from real repair failure using the state the scheduler already records.

siblings.expected_result: Three write-starts with one verified no-op count as two, do not trip a three-round budget, and requeue to rereview; a real failed repair still counts and returns to repair.

machine_checks.why: Replays the empty-review/no-push history, validates stop-loss and repair-cap accounting plus rereview routing, and preserves real failed repair counting and repair routing.

incidents.what_happened: The product's engine pin moved to zenoforge 302a839 through engine/land-direct-main.sh and the push succeeded, but the pinned engine included #164 (d6eee42), which changed engine/hotfix/hf-start.sh, a file the product overrides. Every converge tick then failed for 27 minutes with 'override changed: hotfix/hf-start.sh; adopt the engine version, re-override, or add a seam, then update the row' and 'converge: 302a839... failed to build or check'; the only fix was a manual re-override.
incidents.root_cause_evidence: engine/land-direct-main.sh preflight (pre-fix) ran only scripts/branch-delivery-preflight.mjs and never the target's engine build contract; the contract and its override guard live in the target checkout's build.json hook (.zenoforge/build/engine-sync.sh, 'override guard failed' die at its build()); engine commit d6eee42 (#164) changed engine/hotfix/hf-start.sh while the product's overrides.tsv row pinned the older blob.
incidents.classic_pattern: A deployment pipeline gates a push on the change's own source suites but not on the consumer's integration contract, so the earliest point the contract is exercised is after the change is already live, where failure is an outage instead of a refusal.
incidents.best_known_solution: The lander runs every converge gate before the push, not just the hook's build and check: when the landing range changes the target config root's build.json pin file or the hook's overrides.tsv, run the hook with --build into a scratch versions root, --check the built version, then the built engine's engine-sync.sh --preflight with the landing product SHA as ZF_PREFLIGHT_LIVE_REF and the optional intended-changes.tsv. Converge and landing share publish-preflight/gates.tsv. A failed gate refuses the push with the guard lines and recovery step. Intended rows require an engine SHA so an old approval cannot authorize a later swap; resolved-config changes that exactly match changed product bytes are reported as product-owned, while engine-side or transformed bytes still require a matching-SHA row. Hook path and pin come from the pin file's own hook/engine fields, so no deployment path is hardcoded.
options_considered: Alert faster at converge time (the existing lag clock and supervisor inbox); rejected: it shortens the outage but still lands a pin known to fail its own build contract.

Keep a copy of each consumer's override table inside the engine repo and check engine PRs against it; rejected: no channel syncs the copy when a consumer re-overrides, so it rots and gives false confidence.

Run the target's build hook at landing time for ranges that touch the pin file or override table; selected: the contract is verified at the only moment refusal is cheap, and the guard's own message names the next step.

siblings.expected_result: A pin bump onto an engine whose overridden file changed is refused with the hook guard lines; a pin bump whose publish-preflight detects an undeclared engine-owned file is refused before push; a matching-SHA intended row passes while stale and legacy rows warn and do not approve; product-owned vendored data changes pass, engine-side changes still block without a matching row, and a gate added to the shared manifest runs in both converge and landing; ranges that touch neither the pin nor overrides skip the build.

machine_checks.why: Runs the extracted lander preflight against fixture product and engine repos. It checks build/check and publish-preflight refusals, matching/stale/legacy SHA-scoped rows, product-owned vendored and direct data, engine-side changes, dropped-file approvals, and that a gate appended to the shared manifest executes in both the landing check and built-engine converge preflight.
